title: RWB-S8-E1020-APP: the allocation-to-deviation boundary, the handler roster, the assignment method and any handler cap have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E1020-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slide 13); legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 3, 4, 5 X4, 7 AC7, 10 and 12; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4, A2.1, A2.4, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v3 T0.2, T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2.1, T5.2.2, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01 and R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21
section: Metadata (Contract dependencies); Sections 2, 3, 4, 5 X3 and X4, 7, 8, 11, 12.2, 12.5, 12.8, 13 and 18
description: (1) No source publishes the contract by which rwb-case presents a NEW case to rwb-deviation at the morning allocation: the ownership map gives S8 two write operations only, TSD S8 T-A.1 repeats those two rows, the S8 row of the connection matrix names Temporal and events to P3 and never REST, and TSD S8 T5.2.1 states only that DeviationWorkflow is the child of the case started by P3, so the element names of the case input and of the stage outcome have no baseline. (2) The handler candidates of a deviation are the members of the deviation handler queue, and queue_member and capacity_cap are P3's rows with no published element for this read. (3) The assignment method among handlers is not published: R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06 name the role that owns the code and no source gives a method, a round-robin cursor or a tie-break for deviations, while the legacy key gives a method and a cap to the case owner only. (4) No source gives a caseload cap for a deviation handler, so the placement applies none. (5) The handler queue code "DEV-HANDLER" is the value legacy section 3 records as assumed under DL23 and no published parameter row fixes its reference-data home. (6) The role codes behind the FSD role names are the TSD S8 T6.1 rows, and the FSD names the roles only, so the mapping of a code rule to a role code rests on those two rows.
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S8-E1020-APP: H empty and C = RWB-P3-E1020-CON only, acs empty, secondary true; context pack S8 ownership rows (one table deviation, two operations POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, events EV-06 and EV-07, no job, one workflow) and connection-matrix row S8 (events to P3, REST and events to P1, Temporal and events to P10); TSD S8 T5.2.1 (DeviationWorkflow as the child of the case, started by P3) and T5.2.2 (the consumed rows of the service); TSD S8 T-A.1 (two endpoints, Case record U); legacy RWB-E1-020 section 3 (parameter allocation.deviation.queue.code = "DEV-HANDLER", assumed value, DL23), section 4 step 3 (deviation_open branch), section 5 X4 and section 7 AC7; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 (R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02, R-DEV-03 and BR-S8-004) and A2.4.3.3 (the four roles); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21
proposed: Publish the case element and the stage outcome of RWB-P3-E1020-CON with their field names; publish the queue-and-members element behind the same contract; record the handler choice as the named owner of the fired rule with the fewest open deviations in this service's own rows and no cap until a source sets one; carry "DEV-HANDLER" as a parameter row read through the rwb-case parameters contract; and confirm the role codes of the four handler roles against TSD S8 T6.1 before the contract is tagged

title: RWB-S8-E1020-APP: the key has no contract story of its own, the event names are taken from the TSD, and the business wave is earlier than the service wave
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.6, R5.7, R7.1, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E1020-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row wave 2, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8, 13 and 41); legacy RWB-E1-020 header, sections 1, 2 and 12; TSD S8 Deviation handling v3 T0.1, T0.2, T0.3, T5.2.1, T5.3 and T6.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 DEV route set
section: Metadata (Depends on, Wave, Release, Service epic); Sections 2, 3, 10, 12.1, 12.3, 12.9, 13 and 18
description: (1) The plan gives this key H = None, so no contract story of the key exists and the two published operations of the service are the service baseline's: no element of this key, no fakes of its own and no tag of its own. (2) The ownership map carries the event ids EV-06 and EV-07 without names; the names DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared and their consumer lists are the TSD S8 T0.2, T5.2.1 and T5.3 rows, so the pairing of id to name is an assumption. (3) The business epic is EP01, whose W-MAP wave is 1, while Arch v5 slide 41 and the context pack put rwb-deviation in service wave 2: R5.6 keeps the earlier W-MAP wave and raises one conflict per service and business epic, so the metadata keeps wave 1 and the conflict is recorded here rather than in the metadata. (4) The release date 30 November 2026 is earlier than the service's own wave, is copied unchanged and is marked tentative; a date is never raised as a gap. (5) The platform contracts behind the DP rows of this key are wave 0 stories that the plan does not carry in the H row, so they are preconditions already in place and not in-lane build dependencies.
evidence: Split plan slice RWB-S8-E1020-APP: H empty, C = RWB-P3-E1020-CON, wave 1, release 30 November 2026, business epic EP01, service epic RWB-SVC-S8, patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP14, DP15 and DP19; context pack service row (wave 2) and ownership rows (EV-06, EV-07 without names); TSD S8 T0.1 (service identity and wave 2), T0.2 (EV-06 DeviationRaised, EV-07 DeviationCleared), T5.2.1 (consumers rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-treatment) and T5.3; TSD S8 T6.2 (authorise through the rwb-access contract, DP-08); Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and R5.7
proposed: Keep wave 1 and the tentative date as the plan gives them and let the S8 and EP01 conflict sit in the register; take the two event names and their consumers from TSD S8 T0.2 and T5.2.1; build this key behind the service baseline with the two published operations unchanged and no element of its own; and treat the platform contracts of the DP rows as wave 0 preconditions until the plan carries them
